page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. This server features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, providing an arm64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, alongside a 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a mix of performance characteristics. Single-threaded operations show notable strength, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier status at 36.33 GB/sec and 17.2 GB/sec respectively. Conversely, multi-core performance is limited by the dual-core configuration, resulting in a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 4005.17 and a poor PassMark CPU score of 2191.41. Memory performance is strong according to the PassMark memory score of 2876.9, though uncached write bandwidth is weak at 25.15 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks perform in the average tier, processing 6.51 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.large offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring local NVMe storage without the overhead of larger instance classes. The inclusion of a 118 GB local SSD provides high-speed temporary storage directly attached to the instance, reducing external storage dependency. However, the low core count and weak multi-threaded performance represent a clear tradeoff for parallel processing tasks. This instance is suited for single-threaded utilities, lightweight database operations, static web serving, and basic caching layers.
